minutes_text:
Arts Commission

  Inglewood, California
  April 15, 2026

A meeting of the Inglewood Arts Commission convened on April 15, 2026. Chairman
Jacques Lesure called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m., followed by the flag salute.

Ramara Rubin announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:
   Commissioner Aletha Metcalf, District No. 1
   Commissioner Olivia Alvitre, District No. 2
   Chairman Jacques Lesure, Commissioner at Large
  Absent:
   Commissioner Phyllis Battle, District No. 3
   Commissioner Anya Christiansen, District No. 4

  City Personnel present were as follows:
   Kerri Arroyo  Library Director
   Ramara Rubin  Secretary

PUBLIC COMMENTS.
  a. Shuree Danyell raised questions about public art fund allocations and inquired
  about the decision-making process in selecting a public art consultant.

MINUTES. Commissioner Alvitre moved, and Commissioner Metcalf seconded, that the
minutes for the Arts Commission meeting held on March 18, 2026 be approved.
The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Metcalf, Alvitre, and Lesure
Noes: None

DISCUSSION.
  a. The City of Inglewood Development Services Director Bernard McCrumby
  explained his role, discussed Next Level Inglewood, and provided an overview
  of how the Percent for the Arts Program works. He also clarified Hollywood
  Park operations and offered to arrange a field trip to Hollywood Park and
  share additional information about Hollywood Park’s responsibilities.
   Arts Commission

  b. Monalisa Whitaker inquired about an update on the obligations of Hollywood
  Park’s reflected in the “Champions Initiative”, and the current status of the
  public art fund.
  c. Tracy Michele, addressed the need for transparency and inclusivity in public
  art, emphasizing the importance of local artists.
  d. Shuree Danyell raised concerns about the cohesive style and thought behind
  the city's public art projects, advocating for the consideration of local artists.
  e. Helen Lessick shared information about public art policies and procedures.
VERBAL REPORTS-Public Art‐Related Projects.
  a. Helen Lessick presented a proposal for the Inglewood Artists Pentathlon to
  engage local artists in creating temporary and permanent public art
  installations for the LA 28 Cultural Olympiad.
  It was moved by Chairman Lesure and seconded by Commissioner Alvitre to table
  the discussion regarding the Inglewood Artists Pentathlon until the next meeting on
  Wednesday, May 27, 2026.
  Ayes: Commissioners Metcalf, Alvitre, and Lesure
  Noes: None
  b. Jorge Gomez presented the Inglewood Night Market at Hollywood Park,
  scheduled for September 19, 2026 featuring local artists, live painting, music
  performances, and youth activities. Jorge requested Percent for the Art
  funding to help cover additional event costs.
  It was moved by Chairman Lesure and seconded by Commissioner Alvitre to approve
  $24,800 in funding for the Inglewood Night Market.
  Ayes: Commissioners Metcalf, Alvitre, and Lesure
  Noes: None
  c. Library Director, Kerri Arroyo provided an update on the Inglewood Public
  Library's summer reading program, "Booked on Art," and the upcoming
  events featuring author Sarah McCombie and young author Daisy Huerta.
  d. Library Director Kerri Arroyo provided updates on RFP-0258 Public Art
  Consultant and RFP-0259 Crenshaw-Imperial Branch Library Public Art
  Installation. Kerri reported that selections for both proposals have been made
  and will be publicly announced once contracts are finalized. Kerri also shared
  updates on the maintenance of the “History of Transportation” mural by
  Helen Lundeberg and the status of Rasta Asaru EL’s Utility Box Project. In
  addition, Kerri provided an update on the current public art fund balance of
  $1,309,000.
PUBLIC REMARKS.
  a. Monalisa Whitaker inquired about the status of “The Inglewood Project”
  mural by Richard Wyatt, expressing concern about its preservation.
  b. Tracy Michelle shared updates on the Inglewood Open Studios (IOS)
  Downtown Inglewood Global Village Mural Project and IOS participation in
   the Family Arts Festival on August 8, and requested to be placed on next
  month’s agenda.
  c. Joyce Dallal shared information about the IOS 2025-2026 Willie Stoffer Visual
  Artist Grant Student Showcase opening reception at the Morningside Park
  Branch Library on Friday, April 24, 2026 from 4 p.m. to 5:30 p.m.
  COMMISSIONERS’ COMMENTS/INITIATIVES/ART CALENDAR.
  a. Commissioner Metcalf shared her experience at the Inglewood Public
  Library’s author visit reciting a poem that celebrated the accomplishments of
  Inglewood, emphasizing the city's pride and progress.
  b. Commissioner Alvitre requested a moment of silence in honor and
  remembrance of Bryan Bostic.
  c. Chairman Lesure shared information about a trip to Seoul, Korea, and
  experiences of the city’s art and culture.
  d. The assembly observed a moment of silence for Bryan Bostic.
  e. Next Arts Commission Meeting: May 27, 2026 at 6:30 p.m.
There being no further business to be presented, Chairman Lesure declared the meeting
adjourned at 7:48 p.m.
